takeaway: Hepatic metastases: a past colorectal cancer, weight loss, jaundice, a right upper quadrant mass that moves on respiration and a very high ALP.

question.text: A 62-year-old man has weight loss, jaundice and epigastric pain. He had a rectal anterior resection years ago and now has a right upper quadrant mass moving on respiration. ALP is 752. Diagnosis?
question.say: A sixty-two-year-old man has three months of weight loss, increasing jaundice, and nocturnal epigastric pain. Five years ago he had an anterior resection of the rectum. There is a right upper quadrant mass that moves on respiration, and his alkaline phosphatase is 752. What is the likely diagnosis?

lines.text: Years ago he had an anterior resection of the rectum.
lines.say: Years ago this man had an anterior resection of the rectum for cancer.

lines.text: Colon cancer cells travel to the liver.
lines.say: Colon cancer spreads to other organs. The purple cells travel to the liver.

lines.text: The liver is full of seeds.
lines.say: (sigh) Now his liver is full of cancer seeds.
The right upper quadrant mass moves on respiration.
The alkaline phosphatase rockets to seven hundred and fifty-two.

lines.text: Up to 25 per cent have liver metastases at diagnosis.
lines.say: Up to twenty-five per cent have liver metastases at diagnosis.

lines.text: Remember: a past colon cancer with a liver mass and a high ALP is hepatic metastases.
lines.say: Remember: a past colorectal cancer with a liver mass and a high alkaline phosphatase means hepatic metastases.
